bottleneck.description: One of several Chinese humanoid OEMs (Walker S series) competing with Unitree, Xpeng, Fourier, Agibot domestically and Tesla/Figure/Apptronik globally; no sole-source role in any downstream OEM supply chain.

dependency.key_customers: Dongfeng, BYD, Geely, Foxconn (humanoid pilots); Chinese education sector (Alpha/Cruzr); consumer Jimu kits
dependency.key_suppliers: Inovance Technology (servo motors), ZD Motor (joint modules), Green Harmonic / Leader Drive (harmonic reducers), domestic Chinese precision components

editorial.notes: UBTECH is a humanoid system integrator that pilots Walker S units in Chinese auto plants (Dongfeng, BYD, Geely, Foxconn), but these are pilot deployments, not committed production-line dependencies. The company is a buyer of critical components (Inovance servos, ZD Motor joint modules, harmonic reducers) rather than a supplier of them, so any bottleneck rents accrue upstream. The humanoid OEM market is structurally crowded with multiple peers shipping at similar maturity. This places UBTECH below industrial-robot incumbents (Fanuc/ABB at LOW) on bottleneck dimensions because its end-customer commitments are still pre-commercial pilots.
